newsitem.title: USA: Ecuadoran govt still divided in Texaco case.
newsitem.headline: Ecuadoran govt still divided in Texaco case.

text.p: The Ecuadoran government still seems to be divided over a long-running environmental lawsuit against Texaco Inc, sources said Monday.

Ecuador's Ambassador to the U.S. Hugo Caicedo said in a press release Monday that Attorney General Leonidas Plaza's statements on Jan 23 concerning the case do not reflect the government's official position.
"According to the Constitution of Ecuador, the only Ecuadorian official with international authority is the President of the Republic, Abdala Bucaram," the ambassador said in the statement.

The statement, which reiterates a similarly worded announcement on Friday, undermines the Ecuadoran plaintiffs' efforts to present a united front before the U.S. district court judge in White Plains, NY., where the case was filed, sources said.

Plaza said last week that his government was supporting the Ecuadoran plaintiffs in the case. He denounced Texaco for "irrational exploitation" and "only looking at the profit factor" without taking any environmental precautions.
Politics continues to color this case, sources said. In a separate matter, Plaza has been accused in Ecuador of taking bribes at the expense of the victims of a recent plane crash in the country.

"The position of the attorney general (in the Texaco case) is contrary to the official position, and he's doing it to increase his political prestige" in light of the scandal surrounding the plane crash, former Energy and Mines Minister Fernando Santos told Reuters.

Politics could also play a role in President Bucaram's position on the case, sources said, because the president's cousin, Rene Bucaram, served as manager of the Texaco-operated consortium with state-owned Petroecuador for nine years beginning in 1978.
Texaco is accused of environmental degradation during its operations in Ecuador's Amazon region from 1964 to 1992.
